feature.summary: Shows a coding session's pull request (number, link, state, check status) and lets the person push and open one. A tests button runs the folder's test command and shows pass or fail with output. In the CLI, /recap asks the model to summarise the session. Check status shows on web local, web cloud and mobile cloud sessions.

purpose.what_it_does: For local sessions on the desktop it reads the branch's pull request from GitHub through our servers, shows 'Pull request #N · state · checks ...' as a link, and can push and open a pull request. For cloud sessions on web and mobile it shows checks with failed check names. The tests button runs the detected test command on the computer. In the CLI, /recap turns the session into a written summary.
purpose.why_it_exists: Finishing a coding session means a reviewed, tested change. People need the pull request and results where they work (S66.36-S66.39).
problems_solved: Leaving the app to find the pull request.
Forgetting what a long session did.
use_cases: After a local session press 'Push and open a pull request'.
Press 'Run tests' and read the failing output.
Run /recap in the terminal interface before closing.

where_to_find_it: Desktop-hosted web local session: changes side panel shows the pull request block (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalChangesPanel.tsx:383) and a header button with the label 'Run tests' / 'Stop tests' (LocalSessionPanel.tsx:1129-1141; labels in local-code.ts).
Web cloud sessions: changes panel with PullRequestChecks (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeChangesPanel.tsx:142-210).

Mobile cloud code session: 'Create pull request' action, a pull request link and checks line with refresh (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/useCloudCodeChanges.ts:128-152; CloudCodeChangesSheet.tsx:231-293; CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:364-502).
Mobile remote (companion) code sessions and VS Code: no pull request or test panel found.
prerequisites: GitHub connected through the AGI GitHub App for lookups and opening (apps/web/app/api/code/local-pull-requests/route.ts:21-27).
Local: a git remote and a current branch; the base branch must be known.
Tests: a test command that detectTestCommand can find.
screens_and_controls: Pull request chip: 'Pull request #N · open · checks passing' (local-code.ts:384-411).
'Push and open a pull request', 'Create branch and open pull request', 'Open a pull request on GitHub' (compare link when GitHub is not connected), and a reauthorize link after a failed open.

Cloud/mobile check wording: 'Checks passing', 'Checks failing', 'Checks running', 'No checks reported', 'Check status is unavailable', 'Refresh the checks' (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/presentation.ts:326-331).
journey: 2. Open the changes panel; the pull request block loads the branch state.
3. If none exists press 'Push and open a pull request'; the app pushes, then opens it.
4. The chip shows number, state and checks; checks poll every 30 seconds while running.
5. Press 'Run tests' to run the project's test command; read the message and output.
6. In the CLI run /recap for a summary.
feedback_and_outputs: Not connected: 'Open a pull request on GitHub' link and a text asking to connect (local-code.ts:223-225).
Read failure: 'The pull request for this branch could not be read.'; open failure: 'The pull request could not be opened.' (local-code.ts:231-232).
Tests: '<command> passed.', '<command> failed ...', '<command> ran past its time limit and was stopped.', 'The tests could not be started.' (local-code.ts:57-63).
Recap: a model-written answer in the chat.

Check status states passing, failing, pending, none are computed from GitHub check runs (apps/web/lib/github-app.ts:1384-1392).
Cloud session pull request creation POST and status GET (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/pull-request/route.ts:49; .../status/route.ts:33), shown on web and on mobile.

not_available: Mobile companion (remote desktop) sessions: no pull request or test panel found.
CLI: no test results panel or pull request panel found.
Brief says CI status is missing in every app; code shows check state on web local, web cloud and mobile cloud.

established.statement: The workspace shows the session's pull request (open one, see number, link and state).
The workspace shows CI check status for the session's branch or pull request.
The workspace shows test results: pass or fail, counts and failing output.
The user gets a recap: goal, decisions, files touched, checks run, next steps.
The pull request lookup reports whether GitHub is connected; if not, the person is told to connect.
A failed lookup shows a message, not an empty state.
No second test or task panel in VS Code.

acceptance_criteria: Not connected: lookup returns connected false and the page shows the compare link and the connect text.
Connected, no pull request: the button 'Push and open a pull request' is enabled except on the base branch.
After opening, the chip shows the number and state and links to GitHub in a new tab.
Pending checks re-read after about 30 seconds until they settle.
A GitHub token problem on open shows an error and the reauthorize link.
Tests: a passing run says '<command> passed.'; a non-zero exit says failed with the exit code; a timeout is never a pass.
/recap in the CLI sends the recap prompt for 'this session' or the given focus.
Stop tests ends a running test.
inferred: Because test outcome 'unknown' is recorded for timeouts, validation summaries never claim a pass over a timeout [inferred from use-local-tests.ts:44-52].
proposed: [proposed] Show test counts and failing test names as a panel.
[proposed] Keep a saved recap with the session instead of a one-off answer.
[proposed] Show check status in the mobile companion and VS Code via the same API.

steps.what_happens: The page asks the desktop host for the branch list and remote URL.
The page sends remote URL, head and base to our server.
Our server checks the GitHub App is available and reads the pull request with the user's connection; if not connected it returns a compare link.
GitHub is asked for the pull request and its check runs.
Open: the host pushes the branch, then the server opens the pull request through GitHub and writes an audit event.
Tests: the page detects the command and runs it in the folder through the desktop shell, which asks and sandboxes it.
CLI /recap sends a prompt to the session's model and prints the answer.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Pull request and checks use no model. Pull request creation for cloud sessions may include a model-written description [unknown]. /recap uses the session's model like any prompt (SYS-chat-turn-pipeline).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account and a GitHub connection through the AGI GitHub App. If not connected the person gets a compare link (route.ts; cloud-code-local-pull-request.ts:168).
access_and_usage.permissions: GitHub installation access; a 'reconnect required' reason is passed to the page (local-pull-request-api.ts:13,50-52).
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for the local pull request route. Cloud session pull requests need the managed Code gates (pull-request/route.ts:22-33).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Lookups use the 'default' rate limit and opens use 'chat-conversation' per user (route.ts:38-41,60-62).
access_and_usage.flags: Cloud: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY, and the managed compute private-beta switch (pull-request/route.ts:22-33). The route also needs the GitHub App configured (route.ts:21-27).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: none found in the code, except /recap which works with any model.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Pull requests are GitHub only (GitHub remote patterns in apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/handoff/route.ts:27-31 show the same assumption).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Tests run fully on the device. The pull request lookup and opening still call our servers and GitHub, so they need the network and a signed-in account; this is not local-only.

corrections.claim: CLI /recap sends a summary prompt to the model; the 'goal, decisions, files, checks, next steps' brief is the prompt's wording (claude_parity.rs:1949-1955)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Dispatch and prompt exist, but the prompt wording is 'current objective, decisions made, files or commands touched, verification already run, open risks, and the next concrete actions'. It adds open risks. It does not say 'goal' or 'checks'.
corrections.correction: The brief's items are not the prompt's wording. The prompt asks for objective, decisions, files or commands touched, verification run, open risks and next actions.

corrections.claim: Cloud pull requests need the managed Code switch and compute gate: both checked in the route (pull-request/route.ts:22-33)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The open (POST) route checks e2bProvisioningReady() (needs AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, a non-empty E2B_API_KEY and sandboxComputeIsPriceable) and isManagedComputePrivateBetaEnabled(). That second check is on unless the env var is 0, false or off, so it works as a kill switch. The status GET route has neither gate, only the chat-conversation rate limit.
corrections.correction: Only creating a cloud pull request is gated. It needs the E2B cutover flag, the E2B key, a priceable compute rate and the managed-compute switch, which is on unless set to 0, false or off. Reading checks status is not gated. The page's 'AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY' list omits the priceable-compute condition.

corrections.claim: Run tests control is a header button 'Run tests' / 'Stop tests' (LocalSessionPanel.tsx:1129-1141)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The button renders only when !remoteSsh. A session over SSH has no Run tests button. The button is icon-only (ListChecks), and the label is its aria-label and title.
corrections.correction: The icon-only Run tests / Stop tests header button is hidden in remote SSH sessions. The page's edge-case table omits this state.

missing_facts: The managed-compute switch is a kill switch that is on by default. It turns off only when set to 0, false or off (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:55-58). The page calls it a 'private-beta switch' without saying that, and without saying that e2bProvisioningReady also needs sandboxComputeIsPriceable (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-28).

The cloud pull-request status route (the one behind web and mobile checks) has no E2B or managed-compute gate. It is signed-in, per-user 'chat-conversation' rate limit only (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/pull-request/status/route.ts:14-31). Section 7 lumps it under the cloud gates.

Opening a local pull request needs write access to the repository. repositoryAccess calls assertRepositoryIsWritable for 'open' and requests a token with contents:read and pull_requests:write, while lookup only asks for pull_requests:read (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-local-pull-request.ts:20-23,81-98). The page's Permissions row mentions only 'reconnect required'.
